arxiv-2107-00119.title: Analytical Solution to Electron Beam Envelope Evolution in a Plasma Wakefield
arxiv-2107-00119.creator: Jiayang Yan \corref cor1, Audrey Farrell, Lígia Diana Amorim, Navid Vafaei-Najafabadi
arxiv-2107-00119.description: Abstract Beam-induced ionization injection (B-III) is currently being explored as a method for injecting an electron beam with a controlled density profile into a plasma wakefield accelerator (PWFA). This process is initiated by the fields of an unmatched drive beam where the slice envelope reaches its minimum value, the “pinch”.

arxiv-2110-00533.title: Relative Contagiousness of Emerging Virus Variants: An Analysis of the Alpha, Delta, and Omicron SARS-CoV-2 Variants Thanks: Thanks to Torben Andersen, Victor Chernozhukov, Peter Dalgaard, Emily Dyckman, Claus Ekstrøm, Mogens Fosgerau, Ulrik Gerdes, Martin Vinæs Larsen, Serena Ng, Uffe Poulsen, Mort
arxiv-2110-00533.creator: Peter Reinhard Hansen
arxiv-2110-00533.description: Abstract We propose a simple dynamic model for estimating the relative contagiousness of two virus variants. Maximum likelihood estimation and inference is conveniently invariant to variation in the total number of cases over the sample period and can be expressed as a logistic regression. We apply the model to Danish SARS-CoV-2 variant data.

arxiv-2201-08994.creator: Shiwen He, Shaowen Xiong, Zhenyu An, Wei Zhang, Yongming Huang, Yaoxue Zhang
arxiv-2201-08994.description: Abstract In wireless network, the optimization problems generally have complex constraints, and are usually solved via utilizing the traditional optimization methods that have high computational complexity and need to be executed repeatedly with the change of network environments. In this paper, to overcome these shortcomings, an unsupervised deep unrolling framework based on projection gradient descent, i.e.

arxiv-2205-10685.title: Probabilistic Structured Grammatical Evolution
arxiv-2205-10685.creator: Jessica Mégane, Nuno Lourenço, Penousal Machado
arxiv-2205-10685.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Jessica Mégane, Nuno Lourenço, Penousal Machado. The grammars used in grammar-based Genetic Programming (GP) methods have a significant impact on the quality of the solutions generated since they define the search space by restricting the solutions to its syntax. In this work, we propose Probabilistic Structured Grammatical Evolution (PSGE) , a new approach that combines the Structured Grammatical Evolution (SGE) and Probabilistic Grammatical Evolution (PGE) representation variants and mapping mechanisms.

arxiv-2206-11300.title: Resonance production in partial chemical equilibrium
arxiv-2206-11300.creator: Sándor Lökös, Boris Tomášik
arxiv-2206-11300.description: Abstract In high energy collisions, a dense, strongly interacting medium could be created, the quark gluon plasma. In rapid expansion, from the soup of quarks and gluons a gas of resonance and stable particles is formed at the chemical freeze-out and after that, as the system cools down, the kinetic freeze-out takes place and interaction between particles ceases.

arxiv-2206-14817.title: Stellar Distributions Around a Supermassive Black Hole: Strong segregation regime revisited Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2206-14817.creator: Itai Linial, Re’em Sari
arxiv-2206-14817.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Itai Linial, Re’em Sari. We present a new analytical solution to the steady-state distribution of stars close to a central supermassive black hole of mass M ∙ M_{\bullet} in the center of a galaxy.

arxiv-2311-12524.title: ALPHA: AnomaLous Physiological Health Assessment Using Large Language Models
arxiv-2311-12524.creator: Jiankai Tang, Kegang Wang, Hongming Hu, Xiyuxing Zhang, Peiyu Wang, Xin Liu, Yuntao Wang
arxiv-2311-12524.description: Abstract This study concentrates on evaluating the efficacy of Large Language Models (LLMs) in healthcare, with a specific focus on their application in personal anomalous health monitoring. Our research primarily investigates the capabilities of LLMs in interpreting and analyzing physiological data obtained from FDA-approved devices.

arxiv-2311-15402.title: Learning Section Weights for Multi-Label Document Classification
arxiv-2311-15402.creator: Maziar Moradi Fard Paula Sorrolla Bayod, Kiomars Motarjem, Mohammad Alian Nejadi, Saber Akhondi, Camilo Thorne
arxiv-2311-15402.description: Abstract Multi-label document classification is a traditional task in NLP. Compared to single-label classification, each document can be assigned multiple classes. This problem is crucially important in various domains, such as tagging scientific articles. Documents are often structured into several sections such as abstract and title. Current approaches treat different sections equally for multi-label classification.

arxiv-2406-14738.title: Parameter estimation for partially observed second-order diffusion processes
arxiv-2406-14738.creator: Jan Albrecht and Sebastian Reich
arxiv-2406-14738.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jan Albrecht and Sebastian Reich. Estimating parameters of a diffusion process given continuous-time observations of the process via maximum likelihood approaches or, online, via stochastic gradient descent or Kalman filter formulations constitutes a well-established research area. It has also been established previously that these techniques are, in general, not robust to perturbations in the data in the form of temporal correlations of the driving noise.

pmc-10557899.title: CT‐based radiomics model to predict spread through air space in resectable lung cancer
pmc-10557899.creator: Jialin Gong, Rui Yin, Leina Sun, Na Gao, Xiaofei Wang, Lianmin Zhang, Zhenfa Zhang
pmc-10557899.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundSpread through air space (STAS) has been identified as a pathological pattern associated with lung cancer progression. Patients with STAS were related to a worse prognosis compared with patients without STAS. The objective of this study was to establish a radiomics model capable of forecasting STAS before surgery, which can assist surgeons in selecting the most appropriate operation type for patients with STAS.MethodThere were 537 eligible patients retrospectively included in this study.

pmc-10704800.title: Stakeholders’ experiences of comprehensive geriatric assessment in an inpatient hospital setting: a qualitative systematic review and meta-ethnography
pmc-10704800.creator: Íde O’Shaughnessy, Christine Fitzgerald, Christina Hayes, Aoife Leahy, Margaret O’Connor, Damien Ryan, Denys Shchetkovsky, Fiona Steed, Leonora Carey, Colin Quinn, Elaine Shanahan, Rose Galvin, Katie Robinson
pmc-10704800.description: BackgroundComprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA) is considered the gold standard approach to improving a range of outcomes for older adults living with frailty admitted to hospital. To date, research has predominantly focused on quantitative syntheses of the international evidence with limited focus on qualitative synthesis of stakeholder perspectives.

pmc-11460396.title: Determination of the average crystallite size and the crystallite size distribution: the envelope function approach EnvACS
pmc-11460396.creator: Thorsten M. Gesing, Lars Robben
pmc-11460396.description: A procedure to determine the average crystallite size and its distribution using the radial distribution function G(r) of long-wavelength diffraction experiments is presented and tested. Introduction The determination of average crystallite sizes of synthesized samples is an important tool to understand the physical properties of materials, especially if their dimension deviates from the microcrystalline state.

pmc-12579655.title: Fatigue Experience in Oncology; a Targeted Qualitative Literature Review and Novel Patient-Centric Conceptual Model
pmc-12579655.creator: Chloe Carmichael, Cecile Gousset, Danielle Burns, Jordan Miller, Sophie Van Tomme, Helen Kitchen, Harriet Makin, Natalie Aldhouse, Paul Cordero
pmc-12579655.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). IntroductionTraditionally, treatment endpoints in oncology have focused on increasing overall survival and progression-free survival. Although fatigue may be a meaningful outcome measure across different cancers, it is assessed less frequently. To explore the impact of fatigue on patients with cancer, confirm the importance of fatigue measurement and inform future measurement strategies in oncology, we aimed to characterise the patient experience of fatigue and the associated impact on how patients feel and function, including aspects of health-related quality of life (HRQoL).MethodsA targeted literature

pmc-12619708.title: Determining the influence of livelihoods, land access, and location on household food and nutrition security in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
pmc-12619708.creator: Mallika Sardeshpande, Rowan Naicker, Sithabile Hlahla, Onisimo Mutanga, Rob Slotow, Tafadzwanashe Mabhaudhi
pmc-12619708.description: Access to healthy food varies across socioeconomic circumstances such as primary livelihood, and access to shops, land, farms, and cities. We compared household food and nutrition security across households with food-producing and non-food-producing livelihoods, access to farms and non-farm greenspaces, and their location relative to farms, non-farm greenspaces, shops, and urban centres.

pmc-12699371.title: First-principles investigation of the optical and piezoelectric properties of Janus TiOS monolayers
pmc-12699371.creator: Jing Tang, Kaimin Fan, Kun Wang
pmc-12699371.description: Using first-principles calculations, we systematically explore the geometric structures, stabilities, electronic structures, optical responses, and piezoelectric properties of Janus TiOS monolayers to assess their suitability for integrated photocatalytic and piezoelectric applications. The stability of both phases was assessed through formation energy calculations, phonon dispersion relations, AIMD simulations, and elastic constant analyses, which collectively confirm their dynamical, thermal, and mechanical stability.

pmc-12980699.title: Propolis‐Based Hybrid Nanoflowers as Multifunctional Nanozymes: Structural Integration of Polyphenols for Enhanced Catalytic and Antioxidant Activity
pmc-12980699.creator: Cevahir Altinkaynak, Fatih Kirmizikar
pmc-12980699.description: Propolis is a polyphenol‐rich natural resin with well‐documented antioxidant activity; however, its practical application is restricted by poor aqueous solubility and limited stability. Herein, propolis‐based organic–inorganic hybrid nanoflowers (Prp‐Nfs) were synthesized by integrating a propolis extract into a Cu3(PO4)2·3H2O matrix under mild aqueous conditions (0.8 mM Cu2 +, pH 7.4, 25°C, 72 h).

pmc-13105518.title: SIRT or TACE in combination with lenvatinib and PD-(L)1 inhibitor in high-tumor burden hepatocellular carcinoma: a multicenter, retrospective, propensity score-matched study
pmc-13105518.creator: Jingjun Huang, Huimin Niu, Hui Zhang, Mingyue Cai, Zhiheng Wang, Yongjian Guo, Licong Liang, Liteng Lin, Tingqi Yang, Jiabai Huang, Yuchan Liang, Zhaoxiong Guo, Jingwen Zhou, Wensou Huang, Kangshun Zhu
pmc-13105518.description: Background:The combination of transarterial chemoembolization (TACE), lenvatinib, and PD-(L)1 inhibitors (TACE-L-P) has shown improved outcomes in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). This study aims to compare the efficacy and safety of selective internal radiation therapy (SIRT) plus lenvatinib and PD-(L)1 inhibitors (SIRT-L-P) versus TACE-L-P in Chinese HCC patients with high-tumor burden.

pmc-13192491.title: Lumbar Ewing’s Sarcoma Mimicking a Herniated Disc in a Young Adult: A Case Report
pmc-13192491.creator: Hady Ezzeddine, Wendy Ghanem, Rita Saad, Ramzi Moucharafieh, Mohamad Badra
pmc-13192491.description: BackgroundEwing’s sarcoma is a rare and aggressive malignancy of bone and soft tissue, most commonly affecting the pelvis and long bones of children and adolescents. Spinal involvement, particularly in young adults, is exceptionally uncommon and can present symptoms mimicking more prevalent lumbar pathologies such as disc herniation, increasing the risk of misdiagnosis and delayed treatment.

pmc-13321280.title: Box breathing and prolonged exhalation reduces markers of physiological stress reactivity in response to a virtual trier social stress test
pmc-13321280.creator: Matthew J. McAllister, M. Hunter Martaindale, Nate Sutton, Judith P. Andersen
pmc-13321280.description: Acute exposure to psychological stress activates the sympathetic “fight or flight” response, increasing heart rate, respiratory rate, and metabolic activity. High-stress occupations such as law enforcement, firefighting, and military service regularly involve exposure to intense stress and may benefit from interventions that mitigate physiological and psychological stress responses.

pmc-13347770.title: Effectiveness of Manual Therapy Versus Strength Training for Iliotibial Band Syndrome on Pain and Functional Recovery in Runners: A Pilot Study

pmc-13486475.title: Ultra-flexible optoelectronic stimulator converts tissue-attenuated weak light into electrical signals for cardiac remodeling
pmc-13486475.creator: Ruiyue Zhao, Feifan Yang, Tao Yang, Kanghua Li, Ruisi Gao, Xinchang Kang, Qi Chen, Liang Li, Jia Chen, Yi Yuan, Xinyi Chen, Mengxue Zhou, Shengmin Zhang, Jianglin Wang, Chuanbin Mao
pmc-13486475.description: Precise spatiotemporal resolution and wireless multi-site modulation of excitable tissues via optoelectronics offers transformative potential for bioelectronic medicine, yet clinical translation is hindered by the rigidity of conventional silicon-based devices and their reduced performance under tissue-attenuated illumination, where the weak light reaching implants often fails to generate sufficient stimulation voltage.

pmc-13570987.title: The Association Between Psychological Distress and Young People Engaging in Family Violence: A Data-Linkage Study
pmc-13570987.creator: Maddison Riachi, Benjamin Spivak, Troy McEwan, Nina Papalia
pmc-13570987.description: Young people engaging in family violence (FV) have higher rates of mental health symptoms and diagnoses than other young people. However, the presence of a time–order relationship between mental ill-health/psychological distress and a young person’s use of violence towards family members is yet to be determined.

pmc-13646334.title: First‐In‐Human Study of Mirogabalin (BM2216) Sustained‐Release Tablets: Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, Food Effect and Dose Proportionality With Comparison to Mirogabalin Besylate in Healthy Participants
pmc-13646334.creator: Peiyang Song, Hongtao Zhao, Mingxue Zhu, Lei Wan, Yuan Chen, Zhongping Li, Chengyong Tang
pmc-13646334.description: AimTo characterise the pharmacokinetics (PKs) and safety of BM2216 sustained‐release (SR) tablets after single‐dose oral administration under fasted/fed conditions in healthy participants, assess the effect of food and dose proportionality, and compare the single and multiple‐dose PK of BM2216 SR tablets with mirogabalin besylate tablets to estimate the bioavailability.

pmc-13676676.title: Molecular evidence of Bartonella spp. in wild felids from Brazil
pmc-13676676.creator: Clara Morato Dias, Daniel Antônio Braga Lee, João Vitor dos Santos Alves da Silva, Laura Berger Nunes, Joares Adenilson May Júnior, Vinícius Baggio-Souza, Felipe Bortolotto Peters, Marina Ochoa Favarini, Ana Paula Neuschrank Albano, Suelen Dias Segui, Silvia Resende Terra, Flávia Pereira Tirelli, Jo
pmc-13676676.description: Among Felidae, domestic cats play a role as reservoirs for Bartonella henselae, Bartonella clarridgeiae, and Bartonella koehlerae. Despite the well-known relationship between Bartonella spp. and domestic cats, to date, there is still a paucity of reports on Bartonella spp. in wild felids. The aim of this study was to molecularly detect and characterize Bartonella spp.
